questions.html:
Consider yourself an engineer who wants to design a greedy algorithm for a tour company.

The tour company will be given a list of $n$ tourists, each with a positive minimum hotel space requirement $s_1,\dots, s_n.$

The tour company will also have a list of $m$ available hotel rooms with each room $\text{R}_j$ having an area $a_j$ and a price $p_j.$

Assume hotel has enough rooms i.e. $m>n$.

The company wants to assign each tourist $i$ a distinct room such that area of the assigned room $\geq s_i.$

Consider two strategies below. As an engineer, decide that which strategy will allot rooms to tourists such that the total price can be minimized.

$\textbf{Greedy strategy A:}$ Take the tourist with the smallest space requirement. Assign that tourist the cheapest room that meets the requirement. Remove that tourist and the assigned room and repeat until all tourists are assigned rooms. (If no such room exists, output "no legal assignments").

$\textbf{Greedy strategy B:}$ Take the tourist with the largest space requirement. Assign that tourist the cheapest room that meets the requirement. Remove that tourist and the assigned room and repeat until all tourists are assigned rooms. (If no such room exists, output “no legal assignments”).

The optimal solution is a solution that minimizes the total price for the tour companies.

options.html: Strategy A will work for the Optimal solution but strategy B would fail
Strategy B will work for the Optimal solution but strategy A would fail

questions.html:
Given an undirected, weighted graph $\mathrm{G}$ with positive, integer edge weights, we want to find a path shortest path from $u$ to $v$ with the below condition.

The condition is as follows as:

  • If two paths from $u$ to $v$ are of the same cost, we will choose the path with fewer edges (i.e. if there is tie in shortest paths then we break the tie in favour of a path with fewer edges).
  • If multiple shortest paths from $u$ to $v$ have the same number of edges, we can choose any such path.

Let $\text{G}$ be given graph with $\text{E}$ number of edges. We want to add some constant to each edge weight in $\text{G}$ and modify $\text{G}$ to $\text{G}^{\prime}$ such that by applying Dijkstra on $\text{G}^{\prime}$, we get shortest path in $\text{G}$ as specified by given above condition.

That is, let $u \rightarrow s \rightarrow t \rightarrow v$ is shortest path in $\text{G}^{\prime}$ from $u$ to $v$ then it is shortest path in $G$ with least edges.

Which of the following modification is possible to transform from $\text{G}$ to $G^{\prime}?$

options.html: We can add $1$ to each edge weight in $\mathrm{G}$ then the shortest path in $\mathrm{G}^{\prime}$ is the same as the shortest path in $\mathrm{G}$ with fewer edges.
We can add $1/\text{E}$ to each edge weight in $\text{G}$ then shortest path in $\text{G}^{\prime}$ is same as shortest path in $\mathrm{G}$ with fewer edges.
We can add $2 / \mathrm{E}$ to each edge weight in $\mathrm{G}$ then the shortest path in $\mathrm{G}^{\prime}$ is the same as the shortest path in $\mathrm{G}$ with fewer edges.
It is not always possible to get the same shortest path in $\text{G}$ and $\text{G}^{\prime}$ by adding any constant.
